title: Dungeon Siege West - Interview Highlights - Part 1
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_eLkGBx1XiE

Daniel (@dungeondive) works the room at Dungeon Siege West with a microphone, and the result is a short, scrappy field recording of a scene documenting itself. Four conversations, all of them about gear and origins rather than art.

The first performer's music comes out of Warcraft III and the early World of Warcraft expansions, built almost entirely on a single loop from a Casio keyboard through an M-Audio interface — "this is my baby" — and he offers the closest thing here to a manifesto: if you don't have good strings, you don't have dungeon synth. He rates the Casio's PCM strings above any plugin he could stack in a computer. His neighbour works the opposite way, running heavy percussion and backing tracks so he can get on the mic and work the crowd, and admits mid-interview that this is the first live show of his life — he has never played a note on a stage, and Daniel has accidentally captured his first-ever interview on the same day.

A third runs a black metal tape label out of Boston, twenty-five releases deep, and co-publishes Lurker Magazine — tabletop gaming, music and dark vibes — which will cover this very festival in its December issue. A fourth, from Iowa, plays deliberately stripped-down live versions of melodic, minimal material, sampling backing tracks only so he isn't just hitting play.

----

One performer insists the strings make the genre; another builds everything from backing tracks so he can work the crowd. In any hobby, which matters more to you — the tool or the performance?
